places.name: The Historic Cotton Tree
places.what: A national symbol that stood in the centre of Freetown until a storm felled it in May 2023. Locals say returning settlers prayed under it in the late 1700s, and it once towered over a busy roundabout near the national museum.

source.title: Storm fells symbolic 400-year-old cotton tree in Sierra Leone

notNotFound: The 2021 mid-term census (Western Area Urban 606,701) is provisional and publicly disputed (readable pages: Sierra Leone Telegraph, not recorded); the 2015 census figure is used instead.
UNESCO World Heritage Centre pages return 403, so Gola-Tiwai and Old Fourah Bay College (tentative list) were sourced from RSPB, TRT Afrika and other readable pages.
Cotton Tree age is uncertain (Africanews says both 200 and 400 years; Atlas Obscura only 'existed in 1787'); no well-sourced myth-or-fact item was found.
Freetown founding date: sources differ between 1787 (Province of Freedom) and 1792 (Nova Scotian settlers); BlackPast and Britannica-type pages not usable.
Freetown geography (peninsula/hills) and economy beyond the port, and the 1961 independence date of Freetown as capital, were not verified beyond what is recorded.
